title: Customer Request Heuristic Catalogue — November 2026
content:
TL;DR: Lightweight catalogue of repeatable heuristics derived from customer feedback (Oct–Nov 2026). Aim: turn recurring requests into fast experiments and playable fixes. Not a roadmap — a prioritized set of low-friction probes + hypothesized signal-to-impact mapping.

Purpose
- Capture recurring themes across recent CS threads and field interviews that are amenable to short probes (1–3 sprints).
- Provide a simple decision heuristic so PMs/Eng/Solutions can pick an experiment without re-researching the full thread.
- Surface ambiguous asks that need product research rather than engineering fixes.

Notes on provenance
- Sources: 12 customer interviews (Aug–Nov), support ticket dump (CS-logs Oct 2026), three account QBR notes, and Slack thread link (see linked_artifacts).
- Signal weight is heuristic (frequency + severity + closeness to SLA/customer churn). See scoring later.

How to use this doc
- Pick an item from the heuristic list, check linked tickets, and run 1 sprint micro-probe.
- If probe shows >10% latency improvement or >$0.05/token cost saving for the customer's workload, escalate to dedicated spike + metrics commit.

Heuristic catalogue (compact) — each entry: name / when to apply / common asks / quick probes / known caveats
1) "Prefix caching candidate"
- When: customers with repeated prompt prefixes (templates, system messages) and stable session flows.
- Common asks: "Make our bot faster on repeated multi-turn flows"; "reduce token usage for canned prompts".
- Quick probe: enable per-account prefix caching on a small shard (set TTL=5m) and measure median p95 delta for warm vs cold. Tag requests with short hash of first N tokens (N=64).
- Caveats: privacy concerns for sensitive prefixes — need opt-in + audit log. See JIRA-CS-9012 for privacy checklist.

2) "Adaptive batching hint"
- When: high throughput customers with bursty micro-bursts (short requests, high qps) complaining about latency spikes.
- Common asks: "latency spikes during peak"; "cost goes up with small batch sizes".
- Quick probe: implement a client-side header (X-Redwood-BatchHint: delay-ms) and pilot with one customer to test if small delay reduces cost without increasing perceived latency.
- Caveat: changes user experience for interactive flows; needs UI/UX alignment for customers who cannot accept even 50ms added delay.

3) "Fallback model seam"
- When: customers want graceful fallbacks but also strict output consistency (financial/legal domains).
- Ask: "automatically degrade to cheaper model on overload but preserve gist".
- Quick probe: create a policy that swaps to 3B quantized variant after 250ms queuing, log divergence on small eval set (10 prompts) and measure semantic similarity (embedding cosine).
- Caveat: regression risk on hallucination-sensitive prompts. Add canary gating by route.

4) "Cost-transparent token previews"
- When: enterprise teams need faster cost debugging of prompt/response pairs.
- Ask: "show token cost per route and per user for last 7 days in a compact view".
- Quick probe: add a compact CSV export from the console for a single customer (token counts, model variant, date).
- Caveat: sampling; full-history export may be heavy for large accounts.

5) "Prompt drift alarm"
- When: multi-tenant apps where prompt templates are updated by product/content teams and cause quality regressions.
- Ask: "alert us when prompt outputs deviate from expected distributions".
- Quick probe: baseline a set of golden prompts, run daily sampling, and alert on >12% drop in BLEU/ROUGE or 0.2 drop in embedding similarity.
- Caveat: metric selection is workload-specific; avoid noisy alerts.

Vignettes (short customer stories + candidate fixes)
A) FinOps SaaS (mid-market) — repeated invoice-parsing pipeline
- Raw ask: "We see inconsistent line-item parsing at scale; when we cache a header it helps, but costs spike when the parser uses a larger context window."
- Proposed play: "prefix cache + context length hint" probe. Pilot on 10% of traffic.
- Signal to look for: extraction accuracy, tokens per document, cost per doc.
- Owner: Jonah (CS) / Eng: Luca. Linked artifact: github.com/redwood-inference/ops/proposals/exp-prefix-caching.

B) Legal research platform (enterprise)
- Raw ask: "During volume surges our SLAs are breached; we'd accept a deterministic down-grade for non-critical queries but we need auditability."
- Proposed play: "fallback seam + audit log". Add canary route config allowing two-tier fallback with immutable audit records.
- Owner: Priya / Eng: Platform.

C) Chat-first marketplace startup
- Raw ask: "Developers struggle to find the right batching knobs — setting batching too high increases latency".
- Proposed play: "adaptive batching hint + example presets in SDK". Provide three presets: interactive, balanced, throughput.
- Owner: Developer Experience + CS.

Prioritization quick score (frequency*impact) — shorthand
- Prefix caching candidate: 8/10 (high frequency across doc parsing, chat templates)
- Adaptive batching hint: 7/10 (common for high qps SMBs)
- Fallback model seam: 6/10 (high impact but requires safety work)
- Cost-transparent previews: 5/10 (low engineering effort, good customer visibility)
- Prompt drift alarm: 4/10 (needs bespoke metrics per customer)

Open questions / Risks
- Privacy: prefix caching must have a formal opt-out. Legal to confirm acceptable retention (see Confluence link).
- Observability: need a minimal telemetry contract that doesn't overwhelm SRE. Define a sampling strategy before enabling for >1 customer.
- Metrics: what is the canonical similarity threshold for fallback acceptance? propose using embedding cosine + manual review window.

Quick experiments (engineering-friendly tasks) — 2–4 day spikes
- Instrument token-cost CSV export for single-customer console view (spike: SRE + Frontend, 2d).
- Implement a feature-flagged per-account prefix cache with TTL and logging (spike: runtime + infra, 3d).
- Add X-Redwood-BatchHint header handling in proxy and metric plumbing (spike: 2d).

Next steps & owners (short)
- Triage call scheduled Wed 2026-11-24 10:00 PST — invite: CS leads, Eng Platform, DevEx. Owner: Maya.
- Jonah to assemble 3 customer-specific mini-datasets for prefix-caching probe (due 2026-11-26).
- Luca to open PR for feature-flagged prefix cache (branch: exp/prefix-cache). Link to PR in linked_artifacts when ready.
- Priya to draft legal checklist for caching sensitive prefixes (due 2026-11-30).

Notes to self / loose ends
- Keep this doc intentionally lightweight; avoid over-committing to roadmaps. The aim is to increase the flow of low-cost experiments that either (a) unblock customers quickly or (b) surface a true product investment.
- Collect sample prompts for each probe and add them to Confluence under the shared experiment page.

End of catalogue — feedback welcome. Add new heuristics as we observe repeated ask patterns (esp. anything related to embeddings/reranking or cost-per-embedding anomalies).
